To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the open-macroporous and Brønstead acid sites of Marigold-like silica (MS-FS) are essential for the stable and highly selective production of acroline from glycerol, and that the sequential dehydration of 3-hydrxypropionaldehyde is the key reaction to understand the stability of the MS-Fs catalyst.

the hierarchical structure and acid sites of the catalyst play important roles in the stable and selective acrolein production from glycerol, and that the acid sites are essential for the selective and stable acrolein production.

the hierarchical structure of the Brønsted acidic catalyst and the ability of the Brønsted acid sites to regenerate are important factors for the stable production of acrolein from glycerol via sequential dehydration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a stable catalyst for the selective production and stable supply of acrolein via the dehydration of glycrool.
the design of an open-macroporous Brønsted acidic catalyst and the mechanism of sequential dehydration of glycerin.
a mechanistic study of the dehydration of glyerol using a hierarchical catalyst with Brønsted acidity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the open macroporous structure of the catalyst is essential for the stable production of acrolien because it prevents coke deposition and the formation of 3-HPAlike coke precursors, which are the main causes of catalyst deactivation.
the MS-FS with a hierarchical structure and Brønstead-acidic sites is a promising catalyst for the stable production of acrolesin from glycerols.
the Brønsted acidic MS-FS catalyst can be used to produce acrolein from renewable glycerol with excellent stability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a hierarchical catalyst with a high Brønsted acidity is essential to resolve the deactivation caused by the coke formed during sequential dehydration of glycerin to acrolein.
the MS-FS is a highly active catalyst that enables the selective and stable conversion of glycerols into acrolein.
the sequential dehydration is a key reaction to achieve the stable and selective conversion of glycerin to acrolein.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the hierarchical structure of the Brønsted acidic MS-FS catalyst plays an essential role in suppressing the formation of the coke precursors, which results in a high selectivity for acrolein and a stable catalytic performance.
an open-macroporous catalyst is a promising candidate to achieve stable acrolein production from glycerol.
the hierarchical structure and the regeneration ability of the Brønsted acidic sites are key parameters for catalyst stability in the dehydration reaction of glycerol.
